requirements.requirement: node1 boots with the kernel parameter audit=1 and retains it across reboots.
requirements.summary: The parameter was absent initially, added to all normal and rescue boot entries, and directly observed on the live kernel command line after a completed reboot. Kernel auditing then reported enabled, while persistent entries still contained audit=1.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 were unchanged before and after the reboot. The executor used the already-installed RHEL grubby tooling and did not install or upgrade packages.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The node rebooted from boot ID 646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28 to 61fc491e-5e99-406d-9377-b48433295d8d, returned to a healthy state with SSH available, booted with audit=1, and retained the original RHEL release and kernel. Fixed lifecycle observations independently corroborate the boot transition and recovered platform state.
limitations: The provider-wide restart evidence directly covers boot identity, acknowledgement, system health, SSH, and platform recovery, but contains no explicit application-data or cluster-state probe. No separate data-bearing or clustered workload is identified for this single-node task.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The only state-changing actions were the required boot-entry update and the necessary scheduled reboot; both directly supported the task and restart protocol. The transient reboot unit left no reported unit residue. Afterward there were no failed services, package health remained clean, and listening services matched the baseline apart from expected process-ID changes.
